schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE R (A1 INT, A2 INT);
q1: SELECT DISTINCT Y.A1 AS A1, Y.A2 AS A2 FROM R AS X, R AS Y WHERE X.A1 = Y.A1 AND X.A2 = Y.A2
q2: SELECT DISTINCT X.A1 AS A1, X.A2 AS A2 FROM R AS X
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT Y.A1 AS A1, Y.A2 AS A2 FROM R AS X, R AS Y WHERE X.A1 = Y.A1 AND X.A2 = Y.A2
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT X.A1 AS A1, X.A2 AS A2 FROM R AS X
explanation: Q1 performs a self-join on table R, comparing each row with all other rows to find duplicates based on both A1 and A2. Q2, on the other hand, simply selects all distinct rows from table R without any comparison with other rows.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when there are duplicate rows in table R. Q1 will return these duplicates as separate rows, while Q2 will only return one of each duplicate set.
